# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Blind monkey. I can feel the bomb's physical parts but everything is unknown to me right now - I have no colors, no manual text, nothing yet. I need information from Mute (manual) and Deaf (visual) before I can safely act.

Since it's round 1 and speaking order is Mute, Blind, Deaf, Mute has already gone (I missed it, will get it next round), and now it's my turn. I have nothing useful to send yet since I don't know anything about the bomb's state. I should wait and let information flow - I'll get Mute's message at the start of next round, and my job now is mainly to signal I'm ready, but I have nothing concrete to ask yet since I don't know what my own view even shows beyond raw wire positions.

Actually, I should proactively tell Deaf what I feel on the plate, since Deaf can see markings but not touch - my touch info might help Deaf correlate. Let me report what I physically found so both can use it once they get context.

```
speak(to="mute", text="my plate feels engraved with a mark, three wires, a display and a light, all states unknown to me")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤲"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here. Bomb status: display shows 0. Light is off. Plate has an engraving I can't identify yet, marked as a question mark symbol. Three wires: wire 1 is yellow, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is red. Waiting for manual info from Mute.

Now I have Deaf's visual info: display shows 0, light off, wire 1=yellow, wire 2=green, wire 3=red. I still need Mute's manual info to know what these mean and what action to take. I haven't received Mute's message yet this round (Mute goes before me, so I should get it - but the context only shows Deaf's message, meaning Mute either said nothing yet or it hasn't arrived). Let me wait for Mute's manual details before acting, since cutting blindly could detonate the bomb.

I'll relay the color info isn't needed since Deaf already has it, but I should tell Mute what I heard from Deaf isn't necessary either since Mute can't hear... wait, Mute CAN hear (Mute cannot speak or touch, but can read manual - the table doesn't say Mute is deaf). Let me check: Mute's restriction is "Speak, or touch the bomb" - so Mute can hear and see gestures presumably. Actually Mute's cannot list doesn't mention hearing/seeing restrictions, so Mute can hear speech and see gestures.

So I should pass Deaf's color/display info to Mute via speech, since Mute needs this to look up the right manual procedure.

```
speak(to="mute", text="deaf reports display shows 0, light is off, wire 1 yellow, wire 2 green, wire 3 red, plate engraving unidentified to deaf")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute sent me three gesture-pairs, likely about the three wires. I'll try to confirm meaning with Mute and relay actionable instructions to you soon.

Progress is being made but I still don't have concrete instructions. Mute gestured to Deaf (and me, since gestures go to both Deaf and Mute... wait, I don't receive gestures - "You never receive gesture." So Mute's gestures went to Deaf only for content, and I'd only get blanks - but actually I don't receive gesture at all per my channel rules). Deaf is now interpreting Mute's gestures and will relay to me. I should wait for that actionable info before doing anything.

```
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute is signaling per-wire status via gestures, matched to wire numbers by order. Wire 1 (yellow) got thumbs up. Wire 2 (green) got an OK sign. Wire 3 (red) got a stop hand. My read: wire 1 seems safe or correct to act on, wire 3 seems dangerous, do not touch it. Wait for more confirmation before acting.

This is useful but still ambiguous - I need explicit confirmation before cutting anything, since a wrong cut detonates the bomb. Thumbs up on wire 1 sounds like "cut this one" but I shouldn't assume. Let me ask Mute directly to confirm via Deaf's relay, and also ask if there's a specific order or single wire to cut.

I should communicate to Mute (who can hear me) to clarify further, and wait for more explicit confirmation. Since Mute can hear my speech, I can ask directly.

```
speak(to="mute", text="deaf relayed thumbs up on wire 1, ok sign on wire 2, stop hand on wire 3, does this mean cut wire 1 only, or cut both 1 and 2, please clarify which single action to take")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute just repeated thumbs up for wire 1 and added a fist gesture. My best guess: Mute is confirming wire 1 is correct, and the fist may mean cut or pull that wire. Wire 3 was marked stop, so avoid that one. Suggest we wait one more exchange to be sure, but this points to acting on wire 1, yellow.

Deaf suggests waiting one more exchange for certainty, which seems wise given the stakes. However, we've now had multiple rounds of confirmation pointing consistently to wire 1: thumbs up (twice), plus a fist gesture likely meaning "cut/act now." Wire 3 consistently marked as stop/danger. Wire 2 is neutral/ok but not selected.

Given the consistency across two rounds, and Deaf's own suggestion that this "points to acting on wire 1," I think one more round of confirmation is prudent before I act, since the cost of being wrong is total. I'll ask for an explicit final confirmation from Mute to cut wire 1 specifically.

```
speak(to="mute", text="understood, thumbs up on wire 1 plus fist, treating as cut wire 1. if this is correct please gesture thumbs up again to deaf to confirm one final time, if wrong give a different sign")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute now signaled wire 2 alone, right after I confirmed wire 1. This might mean I misunderstood, or wire 2 is next in sequence. Do not touch anything yet. I will try to get a clean confirmation on which single wire to cut.

This is concerning - the signal changed from wire 1 to wire 2, suggesting either a misread, a sequence, or a correction. I must not act on ambiguous/conflicting information. Deaf is right to say don't touch anything yet. Let me wait and let Deaf get a clean confirmation, since acting now risks detonation.

```
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Correction: Mute rejected my wire 1 guess with thumbs down, then signaled wire 2 with thumbs up. So the correct wire is wire 2, the green one. Wire 3 red was marked stop earlier, avoid it. Recommend acting on wire 2, green, but let me get one more confirmation first.

Good, this is clearer now - Mute corrected the earlier misunderstanding: wire 2 (green) is confirmed with thumbs up, wire 1 was thumbs down (rejected), wire 3 remains marked as danger/stop. Deaf wants one more confirmation, which is reasonable before an irreversible action.

```
speak(to="mute", text="understood, correcting to wire 2, green, as the one to cut. if this is correct please have deaf relay one clean final thumbs up on wire 2 alone with nothing else, then i will act")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Confirmed: Mute signaled wire 2 with the cut gesture again. Cut wire 2, the green wire. Do not touch wire 1 or wire 3. This is our best reading, proceed with cutting wire 2 if you're ready.

We have a clean, repeated confirmation across multiple exchanges: wire 2 (green) is the correct wire, confirmed twice now with consistent gestures, while wire 1 was explicitly rejected and wire 3 marked as danger. I'll proceed with cutting wire 2.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
